stem:
Chetan watches a goat eat leaves under a shady neem tree in his school garden in Nagpur and asks how the goat is linked to the Sun's energy.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: The leaves use the Sun's heat alone to make food that later supplies energy to the goat.
When the goat eats the leaves, energy passes from the goat into the plant.
The goat gets energy from the Sun only while it stands in direct sunlight, not while eating in the shade.
Sunlight helps plants make food; the goat receives that energy indirectly when it eats the plant.

teacher.key_rationale: Plants capture sunlight to make food; animals receive that energy through the food they eat, even in shade. A swaps heat for light; B reverses the energy direction; C treats visible sunlight on the animal as required.
